title: Customer-Centric Performance Claims Framework
body:
Purpose:
This working brief is intended to give GTM (sales, solutions, product marketing) a compact, customer-facing narrative and a short evidence checklist to turn technical latency/cost benchmarks into persuasive, credible claims. Focus: how to explain "faster and cheaper" in customer terms (latency SLOs, predictable unit cost, and infrastructural fallbacks) and when to show raw numbers vs. vignettes.

Audience:
- Field sales and SEs preparing discovery and ROI conversations
- Marketing for one-pagers and web copy alignments
- Product managers and benchmarks team for required evidence

High-level claim architecture (3 layers):
1) Headline claim (customer benefit): "Same quality, lower per-interaction cost and more consistent latency for production LLMs." Keep this short and measurable.
2) Support bullet (what we measure and how): list the metric, typical value, and what it means for the customer workflow.
3) Evidence anchor (how we prove it in a sales conversation): direct metric + short customer vignette + a reproducible benchmark link.

Claim examples (ready-to-use primitives):
- "Typically 20–35% lower per-token cost vs. unmanaged cloud endpoints on common chat workloads."
  - Measurement: normalized cost-per-1k-response-tokens using tokenized JSON chat payloads and default batching policy.
  - Proof: 1) internal batch-run on Llama-3-70B q4-int8; 2) sample customer deployment (SaaS chat) with burst smoothing enabled.

- "P95 latency under load: predictable 250–400ms for 4–8k-context user queries at 16 RPS with Dedicated pools."
  - Measurement: p95 measured over 30-minute sustained RPS window with realistic prompt mix (20% long context, 80% short).
  - Proof: rollback-able canary log + tracing screenshot (link in artifacts).

- "Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to compatible cheaper variants reduces error rate during capacity events by ~60% and keeps user-facing latency within 2xSLOs."
  - Measurement: simulated capacity loss test with route policy fallback enabled.

How to turn metrics into customer stories (vignettes):
- Fintech compliance chatbot (mid-market customer):
  - Problem: frequent spikes when market news hits; SLA requirement for <1s interactive answers.
  - Redwood story: Dedicated pools + prefix caching reduces median token count and maintains p95<500ms, leading to 35% lower monthly inference bill on peak days.
  - ROI snippet to use in pitch: "If you expect 1M queries/month with average 300 response tokens, that shift reduces monthly bill by $X (show calculation)."

- Marketplace indexing and rerank (AI-native startup):
  - Problem: high throughput rerank jobs (bulk embeddings + 3x rerank calls per user request).
  - Redwood story: batch-friendly runtime and KV-caching for prefix contexts reduced effective compute by 2.3x, lowering units consumed and enabling same-day scale without adding GPUs.

Sample quick ROI table (to be templated for SEs):
- Inputs: monthly queries, avg response tokens, current cost per 1k tokens (vendor), current p95 latency, target SLO.
- Redwood assumptions: 30% batching and caching lift for conversational workloads; 20% cost-lift savings conservatively modeled; variant fallback reduces outage exposure costs by 60%.
- Output: projected monthly cost and risk reduction. (SEs: fill numbers from benchmark run and customer telemetry.)

Evidence checklist (what PM/perf must provide before claim use):
- Bench run id and date (artifact): raw results for the model family, hardware spec, and batch policy.
- Test harness: open script that reproduces cost-normalized comparison (linkable).
- Latency trace screenshot (p95/p50/p99) for steady-state and burst tests.
- A short customer vignette with anonymized numbers or an explicit redaction template.
- Legal/comms approval note if claim includes specific percentage savings or guaranteed SLO.

Competitive framing (how to contrast without overclaiming):
- Competitor A (managed cloud endpoints): often cheaper at tiny scale but lacks consistent p95 under burst; call out unpredictable tail latency and throughput variance. Use: "more predictable latency and fewer incident-driven cost spikes."
- Competitor B (self-hosted optimized runtime): may match one-off latency but requires significant platform ops; use: "same economics with 0.2–1 FTE ops savings and faster time-to-scale" (only if evidence from customer PoC exists).
- Avoid naming specific numbers for competitors in public materials. Use anonymized comparative language in field decks and point SEs to appendix benchmarks.

Sample sales script snippets (short):
- Discovery: "What are your typical p95 latency targets today and how often do you see spikes that hurt UX?"
- Value prop: "We help preserve tail-latency SLOs while reducing monthly inference units through batching and cache-aware routing — that typically translates into lower unit cost and fewer emergency scale events."
- Proof-close: "We have a 10–15 minute benchmark we can run on your workload that will show realistic cost delta and latency percentiles; if you want, we can include an integration guide for a single-week pilot."

Messaging guardrails (legal/comms):
- Use conservative language for percentages: "typically", "on average", "in our benchmarks".
- Never promise exact dollars or guaranteed percentage savings without a signed Dedicated commitment or documented PoC results.
- When quoting SLOs, reference the exact conditions (model family, context length distribution, and CPU/GPU profile).

Open tradeoffs and unanswered questions (work items):
- How to present quantized model variants in marketing copy without confusing customers (Q4-int8 vs q4f16). Draft simple phrasing and glossary.
- Standardize a minimal benchmark harness that field can run in <30 minutes against customer payloads. (owner: perf-team).
- Should we publish a public "sample vignettes" doc for the website or keep these behind SEs? (ask marketing).

Operational next steps (owners and timeline):
- Perf team: publish canonical run ids and scripts for the claims above (due 2025-02-16).
- SEs: create two templated ROI spreadsheets for SaaS chat and high-throughput rerank (due 2025-02-09).
- Marketing: draft 1-pager tidy copy for "Predictable latency and cost" (round 1 due 2025-02-23).

Appendix: quick reproducibility notes for perf team:
- Use real tokenizers and full JSON payloads (not trimmed tokens).
- Normalize cost by identical model family and same batch policy; report absolute costs and normalized delta.
- For latency, include p50/p95/p99 and a short timeline of load profile used.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep this doc lightweight. SEs need quick copy blocks. Give them 3 lead magnets: 1) Headline claim + 1-line proof, 2) 2–3-sentence vignette, 3) ROI calc template.
- Link up with legal early if we standardize any percentage-based public marketing.

Unresolved: need final wording on "graceful degradation" to avoid implying our runtime prevents all errors.

-- end --
